item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is preferable because it explicitly validates Upload inputs, preserves the existing Add test, and separates multipart correctness from streamed-file retry verification. Both patches nevertheless violate the contract by bypassing FilesService.Add from Upload and by changing Add to buffer every caller-provided body.","reasons":["B explicitly checks both empty fileName and nil content before multipart construction; A relies implicitly on multipartbody.NewFile for those contract requirements.","B retains TestFilesService_Add and adds focused tests for Upload encoding, Add replay, and Upload retry from an os.File. A replaces the original Add test and combines several Upload concerns into one test.","B parses FilesOption values once and passes the resulting configuration to its internal helper, while A forwards the variadic options through another layer.","B has tighter scope: A adds README and changelog claims about Add becoming replayable despite the frozen contract requiring Add behavior to remain unchanged."],"risks_a":["Upload calls the new private add method instead of routing through FilesService.Add as explicitly required.","Add now eagerly consumes and buffers arbitrary custom multipart readers, changing its existing streaming, timing, memory, and reader-error behavior.","No visible tests cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader errors as required by the contract."],"risks_b":["Upload calls the private add method instead of FilesService.Add, defeating the contract's requested single public path for option handling and error semantics.","Add is changed to eagerly buffer its input, contrary to preserving its existing behavior and potentially increasing memory use for custom bodies.","Its combined validation error is less precise than separate filename/content errors, and no visible tests cover validation or source-reader failures."]}
